cards.text: Psalm 65 is a song by David, written for the choirmaster. It opens in Zion with praise already waiting for God, like bakers lined up at my door before the oven's even warm. Then David tells God, 'to You our vows will be fulfilled.'

cards.question: David calls God 'O You who listen to prayer.' True or false: David says only the people of Zion will come to Him.

cards.text: Then David gets honest. He says there are times when iniquities prevail against him.

cards.question: When iniquities prevail, what does David say God does about 'our transgressions'?

answers.text: He keeps a record of them

cards.text: Now David talks about the people God chooses and brings near to dwell in His courts. Front-row seats, friend. Not the back of a drawer.

cards.question: David says the one God chooses and brings near to dwell in His courts is ___.
The people God brings near get to dwell in His courts. What does David say they're filled with?

cards.text: Now David zooms way out. He says God answers us with awesome deeds of righteousness, and he calls Him 'O God of our salvation'.

cards.question: David calls God the hope of people. How far does David say that hope reaches?

answers.text: To the ends of the earth and farthest seas
To the walls of Jerusalem and no farther
To the borders of Israel and no farther

cards.text: The farthest SEAS, friend, way past where your phone loses its last bar. Then David says God formed the mountains by His power, having girded Himself with might, and me, I need both hands and the whole mustache just to lift a full tray.

cards.question: After the mountains, David pictures the seas roaring and pounding with waves. What does he say God did to them?
True or false: along with the seas, David says God stilled the tumult of the nations.
God calms the seas and the nations. David says those who live far away ___ His wonders.

cards.text: Then David says God makes the dawn and sunset shout for joy. The DAWN, friend, SHOUTING, while most of us greet it by slapping the snooze button.
Now the song comes down from the sky to the dirt. David says God attends to the earth.

cards.question: God attends to the earth. What does David say God does for it?
David says the streams of God are full of water. What does God prepare by providing for the earth?

cards.text: Then David gets right down into the field. God soaks its furrows and levels its ridges, the way I smooth out the dough before the stamp comes down, except He never gets flour in His mustache.

cards.question: The furrows are soaked. David says God softens the ground with ___ and blesses its growth.

cards.text: Then David steps back and takes in the whole year at once. Everywhere God goes, His paths overflow with plenty.

cards.question: True or false: David says God crowns the year with His bounty.
Even out in the wilderness, what does David say happens to the pastures?

cards.text: And David says the hills are robed with joy. The HILLS got dressed up for this, friend, and I've worn the same apron every single day.

cards.question: David pictures the pastures covered in ___ and the valleys full of ___.
At the end of David's song, who shouts in triumph and sings?

cards.text: 'They shout in triumph; indeed, they sing.' Friend, if the valleys can sing about God's goodness, I can at least hum over this tray of chocolate chips.

findings.problem: The question says 'the people God brings near' are the ones filled with the goodness of His house. Psalm 65:4 says 'Blessed is the one You choose and bring near' and then 'We are filled with the goodness of Your house.' The text never says that 'the one' and 'we' are the same people. The question ties them together. Card 5 also turns 'the one' into 'the people God chooses.'

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The setup line 'Now David zooms way out' rules out both wrong answers on card 9 before the baker sees them. Both wrong answers are local limits, Jerusalem and Israel 'and no farther.'

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The two wrong answers share the same shape: 'To the walls of Jerusalem and no farther' and 'To the borders of Israel and no farther.' They mean nearly the same thing. The right answer is the only one without 'and no farther,' so it stands out. The wrong answers should differ from each other and match the right answer's form.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: 'I need both hands and the whole mustache just to lift a full tray' gives Papa Dorin hands. He is a cookie stamper who uses his mustache as hands. This adds something new to his own world.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: Card 1 says God 'attends to the earth.' That setup rules out 'Shakes it and splits it' and 'Freezes it and hardens it.' Neither is believable for someone who attends to the earth, so the right answer is obvious.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The joke 'except He never gets flour in His mustache' gives God a mustache. That makes God part of the punchline. It also blends Papa Dorin's dough comparison with the Bible setting instead of keeping one image.

rule.text: His humor never targets God, Jesus, Scripture or the Marriage Supper.

findings.problem: Card 6 just said God's paths 'overflow with plenty.' The question then opens with 'Even out in the wilderness,' which signals abundance. Together they rule out 'They dry up' and 'They turn to sand,' so the answer 'They overflow' is handed over.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Psalm 65:13 says only 'They shout in triumph; indeed, they sing.' It does not name who 'they' are. Verse 12 also has the hills robed with joy. Making 'The pastures and the valleys' the one right answer settles something the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: 'If the valleys can sing about God's goodness' adds what they sing about. Psalm 65:13 only says they shout in triumph and sing.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.
